Response: the OPERATOR's interactive session -- a human is using the shared install; yield the window, do not touch/restart/re-flag it (a running process's args are not ours to change); free=5.3GiB vs ask 16GiB; outside-scheduler holders: 553489 main.py 17.8GiB (operator-interactive session) -- free 5.3GiB is below the 16GiB ask, and below the harness's fit floor: the ask is not reduced and no render is attempted. A resident co-tenant is not a blocker by itself -- ComfyUI partial-loads the UNet to free VRAM and offloads the rest (it has rendered at a 14.9GiB resident UNet) (card-level peak 23.4 of 24.0GiB measured under contention); card 0% busy over 10s; the :8188 instance is ACTIVELY RENDERING (last prompt 26.8 min ago) -- a batch is driving the card, not idle residue TWO things must be true before the harness can render through that session, and only the operator can make either true. (1) LAUNCH ARGS: an instance carrying the SAME `--reserve-vram` flag as the harness's own launch line (`bin/comfyui_harness.sh plan` prints the exact args, default `--reserve-vram 5`) is ADOPTED instead of yielded to, so the loop resumes as soon as that session has room; without the flag every tick refuses on the launch args even when the card is otherwise empty. (2) THE CARD ITSELF: the flag alone is NOT sufficient while the instance HOLDS its models -- an adopted instance still has to clear the scheduler's fit floor, and a resident ~17GiB hold leaves free below the 16GiB floor, so `poll` refuses `vram_insufficient` (measured 2026-09-22 14:00:41: a FLAGGED foreign instance, pid 3662070, 17074MiB held, WAS adopted and the 16GiB claim was refused at free=6413MiB -- nothing rendered). Closing that instance, or freeing its model cache (ComfyUI's own 'Free model and node cache', or POST /free), returns ~23GiB to the card and the next tick renders.
